stories.headline: Holding the world accountable for the climate crisis
stories.summary: The Dhaka Tribune editorial says that as world leaders assemble in Antalya, Türkiye, for COP31, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, the threat of climate change has long ceased to be an abstract danger, and the world must now be held accountable for the climate crisis. The editorial presents the Antalya summit as the forum where that accountability is due.
stories.why_it_matters: COP31 in Antalya is the year's central climate negotiation, and BCS/Bank climate questions test summit hosts, the COP process and the accountability debate, so the editorial gives students the accountability framing for the Antalya round.
stories.exam_facts: Published 8 November 2026 in the Dhaka Tribune as an editorial; COP stands for the Conference of the Parties, the United Nations climate talks; the editorial's headline frames the issue as holding the world accountable for the climate crisis; the summit gathers world leaders in Antalya, Türkiye, for the 31st session of the conference.
stories.exam_relevance: Climate summits, the COP process, editorial analysis — BCS/Bank environment and current-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: World leaders assembling for COP31 (not individually named in the editorial lede)
stories.figures: COP31; 31st UN Climate Change Conference; Antalya, Türkiye.

stories.headline: Minister says Hasina will never return; Rizvi says people will never welcome her back
stories.summary: Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan said on 8 November that Sheikh Hasina will never return to Bangladesh, warning that attempts to destabilise the country through sabotage will not be tolerated. At a Dhaka University event marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day on 7 November, BNP acting secretary-general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said Hasina, issuing threats from India, imagines crowds greeting her with drums and applause, but the people will never accord her a reception.
stories.why_it_matters: The Hasina return question links the July 2024 uprising, the 7 November observance and Bangladesh-India relations, so BCS/Bank questions on post-uprising politics, BAKSAL and the National Revolution and Solidarity Day draw directly on these statements.
stories.exam_facts: Rizvi spoke at a discussion organised by the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) at the TSC auditorium of Dhaka University on 8 November 2026; he is BNP acting secretary-general and Political Adviser to the Prime Minister; he said Hasina crafted a far more terrifying incarnation of BAKSAL, the system her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman established; he said every sphere of the state was brought under her absolute control and the regime weaponised law enforcement agencies; he said the July 2024 Mass Uprising ended 17 years of rule during which observance of 7 November was prohibited; he said 7 November began multi-party democracy and a foreign policy free from external influence.
stories.exam_relevance: Post-uprising politics, BAKSAL, 7 November, Bangladesh-India relations — recurring BCS/Bank topics.
stories.key_people: Ahmed Azam Khan, Liberation War Affairs Minister; Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, BNP acting secretary-general and Political Adviser to the Prime Minister; Sheikh Hasina
stories.figures: 7 November — National Revolution and Solidarity Day; 17 years of rule; July 2024 Mass Uprising.

stories.headline: Machine learning identifies high-risk paratransit drivers in Gazipur
stories.summary: A machine-learning framework identifies high-risk paratransit drivers in Gazipur, Bangladesh, with regularised logistic regression beating complex ensembles: it scored a mean F1 of 0.557 and AUC-ROC of 0.751. The study interviewed 507 drivers at nine stations in July–December 2021; 121 drivers (23.9%) were repeated-accident drivers and 386 (76.1%) single-accident drivers, in a sector carrying about 60% of motorised trips in smaller cities.
stories.why_it_matters: Road safety, informal transport and applied AI are all BCS/Bank topics, and the study's counter-intuitive finding — the simplest model won — is the kind of result examiners ask about, with Gazipur's 60% paratransit share as the background fact.
stories.exam_facts: Paratransit covers auto-rickshaws, easy bikes, CNG auto-rickshaws, legunas, tempos and manual rickshaws; the study compared five algorithms — Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting and a Stacking Ensemble — using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation, repeated 10 times; the Stacking Ensemble had the best calibration with a Brier score of 0.204 but lower accuracy; the sample included no drivers with zero accidents, a limitation the authors acknowledge; drivers often enter with minimal licensing, training or regulatory oversight; the method generates synthetic examples of the minority class to balance training data.
stories.exam_relevance: Applied AI, road safety, informal transport — BCS/Bank science and current-affairs topics.
stories.key_people: Researchers (not individually named in the report)
stories.figures: 507 drivers; 121 repeated-accident (23.9%), 386 single-accident (76.1%); F1 0.557; AUC-ROC 0.751; Brier 0.204; ~60% of motorised trips.

stories.headline: Titumir: anyone saying ‘December is at the door’ has no connection with Bangladesh
stories.summary: Prime Minister's finance adviser Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir said anyone claiming ‘December is at the door’ for the Awami League's return has no connection with Bangladesh's soil, grass or water. Speaking at a seminar on the 1974 famine at the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum, he argued the famine came not only from food shortage but from the state's estrangement from the people, a crisis of legitimacy and violence — a pattern he traced from 1972–75 to 2009–24.
stories.why_it_matters: The 1974 famine, its three standard explanations and the governance reading Titumir offers are staple BCS written-question material, and the December-return claim ties the famine debate to the live question of the Awami League's future.
stories.exam_facts: Titumir is a professor in the Department of Development Studies at Dhaka University; the discussion was the fifth instalment of the museum's Democratic Journey Seminar Series; he said three theories explain the 1974 famine — falling food availability, lack of purchasing power or access, and the absence of a social contract — plus international food aid and Cold War geopolitics; he said both 1971–75 and 2009–24 saw opposition suppressed, state power abused and patronage reaching from villages to the centre, including in rationing; international rice prices rose from US$147 per tonne in 1972 to $542 in 1974 while Bangladeshi market prices also rose.
stories.exam_relevance: 1974 famine, food policy, governance and patronage — core BCS history and economics topics.
stories.key_people: Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Prime Minister's finance adviser and Dhaka University professor
stories.figures: US$147 per tonne (1972) to $542 (1974); 1972–75 and 2009–24 compared; 1974 famine.

stories.headline: Government outlines three reforms to fix flaws in previous GDP calculations
stories.summary: A joint Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies and planning ministry study found serious flaws and data inconsistencies in GDP calculations under the previous government, prompting three reforms — international standards and geospatial tracking, a scientific method to identify genuine safety-net beneficiaries, and a merged identity and civil-registration database system. Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury said manipulating statistics deceives the government itself; adviser Titumir cited a boat census that reported 13,000 engine-powered boats where a later count found 267,000.
stories.why_it_matters: GDP methodology, BBS independence and the boat-census gap are exactly the statistics-and-governance facts BCS/Bank papers test, and the 13,000-versus-267,000 discrepancy is the memorable number that anchors the whole reform story.
stories.exam_facts: The review was discussed at a National Statistics Day 2026 event on 8 November; Finance Adviser Rashed Al Titumir said statistics were allegedly weaponised to mislead the public and past GDP estimates lacked a reliable empirical basis; the minister said the review aims to identify problems and correct them, not assign blame; the government will ensure full independence of the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) and make reliable official data accessible to the public, who are its rightful owners; greater public access is meant to encourage feedback and expose errors.
stories.exam_relevance: GDP, national statistics, BBS, Digital Public Infrastructure — core BCS/Bank economy topics.
stories.key_people: Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance and Planning Minister; Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Finance Adviser
stories.figures: 13,000 boats reported vs 267,000 counted; 3 reforms; National Statistics Day 2026, 8 November.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Bank orders minimum cash margins on 10 Ramadan imports
stories.summary: Bangladesh Bank's circular of 8 November told banks to charge the minimum cash margin on letters of credit for 10 Ramadan essentials — rice, wheat and flour, onions, lentils, edible oil, sugar, chickpeas, peas, spices and dates — and to give the highest priority to opening the LCs so supplies hold and prices stay affordable. The order, under Section 45 of the Bank Company Act, takes immediate effect until 15 March 2027, replacing a 100% margin rule from 5 September 2024.
stories.why_it_matters: LC margins, Ramadan demand and Section 45 of the Bank Company Act are core Bank-job topics, and the 10-item list with ‘wheat and flour’ as one item is the exact list examiners can ask candidates to reproduce.
stories.exam_facts: The 10 commodities are rice, wheat and flour, onions, lentils, edible oil, sugar, chickpeas, peas, spices and dates. The circular went to the managing directors and chief executive officers of all scheduled banks; an LC margin is the cash or security an importer deposits when opening a letter of credit, and at 100% the importer must deposit the full import value; a lower margin frees traders' capital so small and medium importers can import more, lifting supplies and steadying prices; on 11 November 2025 banks were already told to keep margins at a minimum for Ramadan demand, an instruction in force until 31 March 2026; demand for chickpeas, lentils, edible oil, sugar, spices and dates rises several times in Ramadan, with iftar and sehri meals and large iftar parties; some reports shorten the item to ‘wheat’, but the circular's list counts ‘wheat and flour’ as one item — counting them separately is what produced the ‘11 commodities’ headline figure.
stories.exam_relevance: Letters of credit, LC margins, Ramadan prices, Bank Company Act — core Bank-job topics.
stories.key_people: Bangladesh Bank (circular to chief executives of all banks)
stories.figures: 10 commodities; 100% margin (5 Sep 2024); minimum margin from 11 Nov 2025 to 31 Mar 2026; in force till 15 Mar 2027.

stories.headline: BSC recommends 25% cash dividend; Padma Oil recommends 170% as profit rises 21%
stories.summary: State-owned Bangladesh Shipping Corporation recommended a 25% cash dividend — Tk2.50 per Tk10 share — for FY26 ended 30 June 2026, with the record date set for 15 December, even as earnings per share fell to Tk19.11 from Tk20.10 because FY25 included one-off gains from selling two vessels, MT Banglar Jyoti and MT Banglar Sourabh. State-run Padma Oil recommended a higher 170% cash dividend, Tk17 per share, after net profit grew 21.24% and EPS rose to Tk69.47 from Tk57.30.
stories.why_it_matters: Cash dividends, EPS, NAV and operating cash flow per share are the four stock-market numbers Bank-job papers test, and the BSC–Padma pair shows the same FY26 season producing a payout cut in shipping and a payout rise in petroleum.
stories.exam_facts: BSC's net asset value per share rose to Tk121.45 from Tk104.84, and net operating cash flow per share more than doubled to Tk25.40 from Tk11.96; in Q1 FY27 BSC's EPS grew to Tk5.88 from Tk5.14 and NAV reached Tk127.36 at 30 September; Padma Oil's NAV rose to Tk328.33 from Tk274.86 and its operating cash flow turned positive at Tk63.72 from a negative Tk39.83; Padma's AGM is on 1 January 2027 at 10am on a digital platform, with record date 29 November 2026; Padma's shares fell 0.65% to Tk197.70 on the DSE despite the announcement.
stories.exam_relevance: Dividends, EPS, NAV, cash flow per share, DSE — core Bank-job stock-market topics.
stories.key_people: Bangladesh Shipping Corporation; Padma Oil Company Limited
stories.figures: BSC 25% (Tk2.50), EPS Tk19.11 vs Tk20.10, NAV Tk121.45; Padma 170% (Tk17), EPS Tk69.47 vs Tk57.30, profit +21.24%.

stories.headline: EC plans first-phase elections in 1,000 union parishads on 21 January
stories.summary: The Election Commission plans first-phase elections in around 1,000 union parishads on 21 January, as part of a five-phase programme ending 27 May 2027, EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed said on 8 November. The second phase is likely on 4 February, with later phases on 29 April, 13 May and 27 May, scheduled around Ramadan, the SSC examinations and coastal weather; the terms of around 4,300 union parishads have already expired.
stories.why_it_matters: Union parishad elections, the EC's five-phase calendar and the old-laws-versus-reforms question are direct BCS local-government topics, and the 1,000-UP first phase on 21 January is the date examiners will ask.
stories.exam_facts: Akhtar Ahmed spoke at the Election Commission Bhaban in Agargaon; the five-phase decision was taken at a Commission meeting on 12 October, and Election Commissioner Brig Gen (Retd) Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah earlier confirmed the schedule; lists of UPs for the first and second phases are expected to be finalised by Thursday; all UPs of an upazila whose terms expired will vote simultaneously, and UPs held up by court cases can join if final verdicts come before the final list; the EC is printing ballot papers for chairman, general member and reserved women member posts; The Daily Star reported the polls will run under existing laws, with key electoral and local-government reforms left out.
stories.exam_relevance: Local government, union parishads, Election Commission — core BCS civics topics.
stories.key_people: Akhtar Ahmed, EC Senior Secretary; Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah, Election Commissioner
stories.figures: 1,000 UPs in phase 1; 4,300 UPs' terms expired; phases: 21 Jan, 4 Feb, 29 Apr, 13 May, 27 May 2027.

stories.headline: Ninth teacher recruitment examination to be held in three stages; syllabus may change
stories.summary: The Ninth Teacher Recruitment Examination, run by the Non-Government Teachers' Registration and Certification Authority (NTRCA), may be held in December in three stages — a 100-mark MCQ preliminary of one hour, a 100-mark written test of three hours, and a 20-mark viva voce — with the syllabus possibly revised. For the first time the examination will lead directly to recruitment, not merely certify eligibility, so it is called a recruitment examination, not the 19th registration examination.
stories.why_it_matters: NTRCA, the three-stage format and the 100–100–20 marks split are exactly the kind of recruitment-examination facts BCS/Bank candidates are asked, and the switch from ‘registration’ to ‘recruitment’ is the conceptual point behind the new name.
stories.exam_facts: The preliminary syllabus covers Bengali, English, Mathematics and General Knowledge, 25 marks each; one mark per correct answer, 0.25 deducted per wrong answer, pass mark 40 per cent; the format depends on amendments to the relevant regulations and approval from the Ministry of Education; viva voce examinations for heads and assistant heads of institutions are under way and end on 9 December; the NTRCA last notified the 18th Teacher Registration Examination on 4 November 2023, with the preliminary held in March 2024.
stories.exam_relevance: Teacher recruitment, NTRCA, examination formats — direct Jobs & Education topics for BCS/Bank candidates.
stories.key_people: Non-Government Teachers' Registration and Certification Authority (NTRCA)
stories.figures: 100-mark MCQ (1 hour) + 100-mark written (3 hours) + 20-mark viva; pass mark 40%; 0.25 negative marking; 25 marks per subject.

stories.headline: Import bill up 11.5% in first quarter of FY27 amid global price pressures
stories.summary: Bangladesh's import expenditure rose 11.50 per cent in the first quarter of the current fiscal year 2026-27 amid global price pressures. The Financial Express reported the rise on 8 November, with the upward trend expected to continue in the coming months.
stories.why_it_matters: The import bill is the first hard external-sector number of FY27, and BCS/Bank economy papers test import trends, the trade balance and the reserves behind them, so the 11.50% first-quarter rise is the figure to remember.
stories.exam_facts: The Q1 figure is the first-quarter reading for FY27, the fiscal year 2026-27; the 11.50 per cent rise is measured on import spending, and the report ties it to global price pressures; the upward trend is expected to continue in the coming months; the report was published by The Financial Express on 8 November 2026.
stories.exam_relevance: Imports, trade balance, external sector — core BCS/Bank economy topics.

stories.headline: PM urges new BCS officers to serve people with honesty, efficiency and humanity
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged newly recruited civil servants to serve people with honesty, efficiency and humanity, stressing that no citizen should face harassment while seeking government services. The address to the new officers, reported on 8 November, sets honesty, efficiency and human values as the standard for the civil service.
stories.why_it_matters: BCS is the examination itself, so a prime ministerial address to newly recruited civil servants — honesty, efficiency, humanity, no harassment — is the values question BCS viva and written papers return to.
stories.exam_facts: The prime minister addressed newly recruited civil servants at the start of their careers; the Dhaka Tribune reports the address as Sunday, while The Daily Star dates it to the previous day, so the two reports differ on the day; the Tribune version stresses human values and the Star version stresses humanity and ensuring no citizen faces harassment while seeking government services; the message targets officers entering the civil service.
stories.exam_relevance: Civil service values, BCS, public administration — direct BCS topics.

stories.headline: 300 shortlisted by lottery for zero-cost jobs at Malaysian firm
stories.summary: A total of 300 candidates were provisionally shortlisted through a lottery for recruitment by Malaysian company DHL Supply Chain Malaysia Sdn Bhd at zero migration cost, after 4,029 candidates applied online between 6 November and 4pm on 8 November. Of the 300, 200 were shortlisted for Operations Assistant posts and 100 for Technical Skilled Worker posts; 112 successful candidates will go to Malaysia with the employer paying medical fees and airfares.
stories.why_it_matters: Overseas employment, zero-migration-cost recruitment and the 1-crore-workers pledge are core BCS/Bank labour-migration topics, and the lottery mechanism is the new selection fact examiners can test.
stories.exam_facts: The electronic lottery was held at Probashi Kallyan Bhaban in Dhaka in the presence of ministry officials, BOESL representatives and journalists; the shortlisted candidates face practical examinations and viva voce before the recruiting company's representatives, and the list will be published on BOESL's website and Facebook page; acting expatriate welfare secretary Ahmadul Haque said the initiative supports the government's pledge to send 1 crore workers abroad over five years; BOESL managing director Mohammad Rashedul Haque said it is the first government initiative to select eligible and skilled workers by lottery.
stories.exam_relevance: Overseas employment, BOESL, labour migration — core BCS/Bank topics.
stories.key_people: Ahmadul Haque, acting secretary, expatriate welfare ministry; Mohammad Rashedul Haque, managing director, BOESL; DHL Supply Chain Malaysia Sdn Bhd

stories.headline: Six garment factories in Gazipur's Konabari shut amid wage protests
stories.summary: Six garment factories in Gazipur's Konabari area have been shut following protests by workers demanding higher wages. The Daily Star reported the shutdowns on 8 November.
stories.why_it_matters: Garment wages and factory stoppages are the most tested RMG facts in BCS/Bank economy papers, and the Konabari shutdowns show the wage demand behind the current unrest in the garment belt.
stories.exam_facts: Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amjad Hossain confirmed the shutdowns; the factories are in Konabari, Gazipur; the workers were protesting for higher wages; the shutdowns follow the garment sector's wage protests.

options.B: A fine imposed for late payment

mcqs.explanation: A dividend is a share of a company's profits paid to shareholders — BSC recommended 25%, Padma Oil 170%.

mcqs.question: The word 'syllabus' most nearly means:

options.C: The topics covered in a course
options.D: A school building in a rural area

mcqs.explanation: A syllabus is the list of topics covered in a course or examination — the NTRCA syllabus may be revised.

mcqs.question: In the Ramadan LC story, a 'cash margin' is:

options.A: A tax charged on imported rice and wheat
options.B: A discount offered to large importers
options.C: Deposit paid to open an LC
options.D: The profit a bank earns from lending money

mcqs.explanation: A cash margin is the cash an importer deposits with a bank when opening a letter of credit; Bangladesh Bank told banks to keep it at the minimum.

mcqs.question: The 'record date' in the BSC dividend story is the date for:

options.C: Paying the dividend to all shareholders

mcqs.explanation: The record date determines shareholder entitlement to the dividend — 15 December for BSC, 29 November 2026 for Padma Oil.

mcqs.question: Where is COP31 being held?
mcqs.explanation: COP31, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, is being held in Antalya, Türkiye, where world leaders have assembled.

mcqs.question: At the Dhaka University event marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day, who said the people would never accord Sheikh Hasina a reception?
mcqs.explanation: BNP acting secretary-general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said the people would never accord Hasina a reception if she returned.

mcqs.question: In the Gazipur paratransit study, which model performed best?
mcqs.explanation: Regularised logistic regression was the best-performing and most stable classifier, with a mean F1 of 0.557 and AUC-ROC of 0.751.

mcqs.question: According to Titumir, the international price of rice rose from US$147 per tonne in 1972 to how much in 1974?
mcqs.explanation: The international price of rice stood at US$147 per tonne in 1972 before rising to $542 in 1974.

mcqs.question: The boat census cited by Titumir reported 13,000 engine-powered boats, while a later count found how many?
mcqs.explanation: The previous government reported only 13,000 engine-powered boats, whereas a subsequent count found 267,000.

mcqs.question: How many essential commodities are covered by Bangladesh Bank's 8 November circular?
mcqs.explanation: The circular covers 10 commodities — rice, wheat and flour, onions, lentils, edible oil, sugar, chickpeas, peas, spices and dates. 'Wheat and flour' is one item; counting them separately produced the '11' headline figure.

mcqs.question: What cash dividend did Padma Oil recommend for FY26?
mcqs.explanation: Padma Oil recommended a 170% cash dividend, Tk17 per share, after net profit grew 21.24%.

mcqs.question: On which date is the first phase of union parishad elections planned?
mcqs.explanation: The Election Commission plans first-phase elections in around 1,000 union parishads on 21 January.

mcqs.question: How many stages will the Ninth Teacher Recruitment Examination have?
mcqs.explanation: The examination will have three stages: a 100-mark MCQ preliminary, a 100-mark written test and a 20-mark viva voce.

mcqs.question: By how much did Bangladesh's import expenditure rise in Q1 FY27?
mcqs.explanation: Import expenditure rose by 11.50 per cent in the first quarter of FY27.

mcqs.question: What did the Prime Minister urge newly recruited civil servants to do?

options.C: Serve people with honesty, efficiency and humanity

mcqs.explanation: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged newly recruited civil servants to serve people with honesty, efficiency and humanity.

mcqs.question: How many of the 300 shortlisted candidates will be sent to Malaysia?
mcqs.explanation: 112 successful candidates will be sent to Malaysia at zero migration cost, after practical examinations and viva voce.

mcqs.question: How many garment factories in Gazipur's Konabari were shut amid wage protests?
mcqs.explanation: Six garment factories in Gazipur's Konabari area were shut following protests by workers demanding higher wages.
